info.name: Gymnasyum Backend API
info.description: Ordered happy-path and negative API verification flow for the Gymnasyum backend. Run with the local environment against a development database seeded with the demo admin and catalog service records.

request.description: Public health probe. Expected: HTTP 200 with status "ok".
Public customer registration. Expected: HTTP 200 on first run; HTTP 409 if the demo email already exists.

exec: pm.test("response status is expected", function () { pm.expect([200, 409]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

request.description: Customer login. Expected: HTTP 200; saves accessToken and refreshToken.
Negative invalid-login case. Expected: HTTP 401.

Diagnostic seed prerequisite check only. Expected: HTTP 409 because admin@example.com must already be seeded. If HTTP 200 is returned, registration created a customer, which is intentionally never saved as an admin token; seed the admin account before running Login Admin.

exec: pm.test("fallback registration did not create an admin", function () { pm.expect(body.user && body.user.role).to.eql("customer"); });

pm.test("seeded admin prerequisite is available", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code, "Admin seed is missing: registration returned a customer (HTTP 200); seed the admin account before Login Admin").to.eql(409); });

request.description: Seeded admin login. Expected: HTTP 200 with role "admin"; saves admin tokens only after the role assertion passes. Requires the seeded admin account.

exec: pm.test("Login Admin returned the seeded admin role", function () { pm.expect(isAdmin, "Login Admin requires a seeded admin account; received role: " + (body.user && body.user.role)).to.eql(true); });
pm.test("access token exists for the admin account", function () { pm.expect(isAdmin && body.accessToken, "Admin token was not saved because the response user was not an admin").to.be.ok; });

pm.test("refresh token exists for the admin account", function () { pm.expect(isAdmin && body.refreshToken, "Admin refresh token was not saved because the response user was not an admin").to.be.ok; });

request.description: Refresh token rotation. Expected: HTTP 200; replaces both tokens.
Protected admin identity read. Expected: HTTP 200.
Invalidate the seeded admin refresh token. Expected: HTTP 200 with success true; uses the admin bearer token and does not overwrite token variables.
Negative role check. Customer uses admin-only route. Expected: HTTP 403.
Negative ownership check. Customer attempts to read the seeded admin user. Expected: HTTP 403.
Admin user list. Expected: HTTP 200 with an array.
Admin reads seeded customer user. Expected: HTTP 200.
Admin updates the seeded customer user name. Expected: HTTP 200 with the updated user record.

exec: pm.test("updated user id exists", function () { pm.expect(body.id).to.not.be.undefined; });
pm.test("updated user name is returned", function () { pm.expect(body.name).to.eql("Postman Customer Updated"); });
pm.test("updated user remains a customer", function () { pm.expect(body.role).to.eql("customer"); });

request.description: Customer reads own member profile. Expected: HTTP 200; saves memberId.
Customer updates own profile. Expected: HTTP 200.

exec: pm.test("updated member id exists", function () { pm.expect(body.id).to.not.be.undefined; });

request.description: Admin member list. Expected: HTTP 200.
Admin reads customer member. Expected: HTTP 200.
Negative role check. Customer cannot create coaches. Expected: HTTP 403.
Admin coach list. Expected: HTTP 200.
Admin creates coach associated to seeded service. Expected: HTTP 200; saves coachId.
Admin updates coach. Expected: HTTP 200.

exec: pm.test("updated coach id exists", function () { pm.expect(body.id).to.not.be.undefined; });

request.description: Admin creates active package. Expected: HTTP 200; saves packageId.
Admin updates the package created by the preceding request. Expected: HTTP 200 with the updated package record.

exec: pm.test("updated package description is returned", function () { pm.expect(body.description).to.eql("Five coached sessions, updated by Postman"); });

request.description: Customer catalog read. Expected: HTTP 200.
Negative validation case. Expected: HTTP 422.
Admin creates capacity-one source schedule. Expected: HTTP 200; saves scheduleId.
Admin creates target reschedule. Expected: HTTP 200; saves targetScheduleId.

exec: pm.test("target schedule id exists", function () { pm.expect(body.id).to.not.be.undefined; });

request.description: Admin updates the source schedule created by the preceding request. Expected: HTTP 200 with the updated schedule record.

exec: pm.test("updated schedule title is returned", function () { pm.expect(body.title).to.eql("Postman Morning Yoga Updated"); });

request.description: Customer schedule read. Expected: HTTP 200.
Negative validation case. Expected: HTTP 422.
Customer creates pending payment. Expected: HTTP 200; saves paymentId.
Customer own payment list. Expected: HTTP 200.
Negative role check. Expected: HTTP 403.
Admin marks pending payment paid. Expected: HTTP 200; creates subscription and saves subscriptionId.
Admin payment list. Expected: HTTP 200.
Customer subscription read after payment is marked paid. Expected: HTTP 200.

exec: const body = pm.response.json(); pm.test("created subscription is present", function () { pm.expect(body.some(function (item) { return item.id === pm.environment.get("subscriptionId"); })).to.eql(true); });

request.description: Customer books source schedule. Expected: HTTP 200; saves bookingId.

item.name: Customer full or duplicate booking rejected

request.description: Negative full/duplicate booking case. Expected: HTTP 409.
Negative malformed identifier case. Expected: HTTP 422.
Customer own booking list. Expected: HTTP 200.
Admin booking list. Expected: HTTP 200.
Customer cancels the booking after the reschedule flow completes. Expected: HTTP 200 with cancelled status. The endpoint has no request fields; an empty JSON object is sent explicitly.
Customer requests reschedule. Expected: HTTP 200; saves rescheduleId.
Negative role check. Customer cannot review. Expected: HTTP 403.
Admin request list. Expected: HTTP 200.
Admin reviews request. Expected: HTTP 200 with approved status and reviewer.
Customer own request list. Expected: HTTP 200.

exec: const body = pm.response.json(); pm.test("approved request is present", function () { pm.expect(body.some(function (item) { return item.id === pm.environment.get("rescheduleId"); })).to.eql(true); });

request.description: Final customer member read. Expected: HTTP 200.
Final package catalog read. Expected: HTTP 200.

exec: pm.test("package response is an array", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.be.an("array"); });

request.description: Final schedule read. Expected: HTTP 200.

exec: pm.test("schedule response is an array", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.be.an("array"); });

request.description: Final payment read. Expected: HTTP 200.

exec: pm.test("payment response is an array", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.be.an("array"); });

request.description: Final subscription read. Expected: HTTP 200.

exec: pm.test("subscription response is an array", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.be.an("array"); });

request.description: Final booking read. Expected: HTTP 200.

exec: pm.test("booking response is an array", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.be.an("array"); });

request.description: Final admin request read. Expected: HTTP 200.

exec: pm.test("request response is an array", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.be.an("array"); });
